title: Chiral superconductors and competing states across a Lifshitz transition in rhombohedral pentalayer graphene
authors: Chuanqi Zheng, Cheng Xu, Chushan Li, Chenyu Zhang, Zijing Zhang, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Hao Yang, Dandan Guan, Liang Liu, Shiyong Wang, Yaoyi Li, Hao Zheng, Canhua Liu, Jinfeng Jia, Shengwei Jiang, Zhiwen Shi, Guorui Chen, Fengcheng Wu, Yang Zhang, Tingxin Li, Xiaoxue Liu
abstract: Rhombohedral multilayer graphene hosts a distinctive low-energy electronic structure in which strong Coulomb interactions and nontrivial quantum geometry intertwine to generate exotic quantum states. Recent experiments reported signatures of chiral superconductivity in electron-doped rhombohedral multilayer graphene within the spin- and valley-polarized regime. Here we map the normal-state fermiology surrounding chiral superconductivity in rhombohedral pentalayer graphene. Quantum oscillation measurements reveal an electrically controlled Lifshitz transition between a simply-connected circular quarter-metal Fermi surface and an annular quarter-metal Fermi surface. The Lifshitz boundary itself shifts with perpendicular magnetic field, consistent with the strongly momentum-dependent orbital magnetic moment of the low-energy band. Approaching the transition from either side, the electron effective mass becomes strongly enhanced, implying the formation of a nearly dispersionless band bottom and a strongly reduced kinetic-energy scale. This singular electronic structure produces a regime of exceptionally strong instability in which chiral superconductivity competes with Wigner crystalline phases and reentrant quantum Hall states. In particular, two superconducting regions with signatures of orbital time-reversal-symmetry breaking lie on opposite sides of the Lifshitz boundary and have comparable transition temperatures, yet the annular-side state is suppressed by a substantially smaller perpendicular magnetic field. Our calculation finds comparable chiral pairing tendencies on the two parent Fermi surfaces while producing a much lower orbital-Zeeman pair-breaking scale and an additional finite-momentum pairing tendency for the annular state. These results identify Fermi-surface topology as a key control parameter for chiral superconductivity in rhombohedral graphene.
summary: This work investigates chiral superconductivity in rhombohedral graphene, showing that the electronic structure undergoes a Lifshitz transition between circular and annular Fermi surfaces. This topological change is crucial, as it dictates the stability and nature of the competing superconducting and quantum Hall states. The findings establish Fermi-surface topology as the primary control knob for realizing and tuning these exotic correlated quantum phases.
main_problem: The study maps the normal-state electronic structure surrounding chiral superconductivity and determines how Fermi-surface topology controls this exotic superconducting state in rhombohedral graphene.
main_result: The Lifshitz transition between circular and annular Fermi surfaces is identified as the key control parameter, leading to two distinct superconducting phases with different magnetic field stabilities.
method: The research combines quantum oscillation measurements (SdH) to map the Fermi surface, transport measurements ($R_{xx}, R_{xy}$) to trace phase boundaries, and theoretical calculations of pairing tendencies.
model_or_system: The system is rhombohedral pentalayer graphene (RPG), an electrically tunable platform exhibiting strong Coulomb interactions and nontrivial quantum geometry.
key_observables: Quantum oscillation frequencies, effective mass ($m^*$), superconducting transition temperatures ($T_c$), and the location of the Lifshitz transition boundary in the $n-D$ phase diagram.
important_parameters: Carrier density ($n$), perpendicular electric field ($D$), and perpendicular magnetic field ($B_{\perp}$); the transition is governed by the Fermi surface topology (Circular vs. Annular).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that the observed superconducting phases are dictated by the underlying Fermi-surface topology near the Lifshitz transition.
figures_summary: Figures map the complex phase diagram showing transitions between various correlated states (CQM, AQM, SC domes) and illustrate the systematic shift of the Lifshitz boundary with $B_{\perp}$.
paper_structure: The paper systematically maps the phase diagram by first identifying the Lifshitz transition, then analyzing the distinct superconducting domes (CSC1 and CSC2) on either side, and finally using calculations to confirm the role of Fermi-surface geometry in determining magnetic field robustness.
why_interesting: The strong coupling between electronic topology (Fermi surface geometry) and emergent superconductivity provides a concrete, tunable platform for studying correlated quantum phases, relevant to understanding unconventional superconductivity in 2D materials.
